column1: # Direct source evidence for the Rust parser allocation boundary.

column5: Rust ports generic default allocation, exact typed batch size, stable distinct typed slots, nullable zero-length slice allocation, reset, and reachability across reset without unsafe byte allocation. The slab retains only its current batch; escaped handles alone keep older batches alive, matching Go reachability. The Rust parser still constructs owned AST values directly rather than consuming dedicated hot-type slabs.
